title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Prop. 2.4, continued from p.61). X and Y are smooth projective varieties over k, and X has dimension n. A_• is the Albanese variety and B_• the Picard variety. A correspondence (the beta/Z of the notes) induces a homomorphism of abelian varieties u = u_Z : A_Y -> B_X. Under the canonical identifications H^1(Y,Q_l) = H^1(A_Y,Q_l) and H^{2n-1}(X,Q_l)(n-1) = H^1(B_X,Q_l), it also induces the cohomological map cl(gamma(beta)) : H^1(Y,Q_l) -> H^{2n-1}(X,Q_l)(n-1). The prototype is the Lefschetz operator L^{n-1}, with Y = X and beta a power of a hyperplane class.

Statement. Fix l prime to char k. Then cl(gamma(beta)) is an isomorphism if and only if u^{(l)} = H^1(u) is, i.e. if and only if u is an isogeny. In that case there is a divisor D on X x Y with rational coefficients such that cl(^t gamma(D)) : H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) -> H^1(Y) is the inverse of cl(gamma(beta)). This determines D as an element of Al(X x Y) ⊗ Q, at least as far as its action on H^1 is concerned. Via Weil's theory of divisorial correspondences, D corresponds to u^{-1}, an element of Hom(A_Y,B_X) ⊗ Q (the quasi-inverse).

Integrality refinements.
- D can be chosen with integer coefficients if and only if u is an isomorphism.
- More generally, if N is an integer annihilating the obstruction (essentially the kernel or degree of the isogeny), D can be taken of the form N^{-r} D_0, with D_0 integral and r >= 0. So the only primes in the denominator are those dividing N.

Proof sketch. Grothendieck writes the commutative square H^1(Y) -> H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) over H^1(A_Y) -> H^1(B_X), with vertical isomorphisms and all arrows 'Z-algebraic' (defined over the integral structures). Invertibility then reduces to u^{(l)}, i.e. to u being an isogeny. The quasi-inverse of u is realised by a Q-divisorial correspondence, so its cohomology class is algebraic. The next page treats the sharpness of the denominator. For the p-part in characteristic p it invokes the effect of correspondences on isocrystals (Dieudonné theory).

Purpose. This is the proof that the Lefschetz-type standard conjecture (algebraicity of the inverse of L^{n-1}, i.e. of Lambda) holds in degree 1, together with an integral or denominator-controlled version.
errors: 'ce qui caractérise D comme élément de Al(X×Y)⊗Q' is too strong as written. Only the H^1⊗H^1 Künneth component of D (D modulo divisors pulled back from X and from Y, and modulo algebraic equivalence) is determined by the induced map. Classes from NS(X)⊗1 and 1⊗NS(Y) act trivially on H^1.
The inverse of u : A_Y -> B_X naturally lives in Hom(B_X,A_Y)⊗Q, while the text writes Hom_Q(A_Y,B_X). This is a direction/transpose slip, harmless up to the contravariance of cohomology.

The denominator statement is garbled ('r ≥ 0 ... mais pas ≥ 1 ?'). If N is the exponent of ker u, then N·u^{-1} is a genuine homomorphism, so r = 1 already suffices for that N. The intended sharp statement about which powers of which primes occur is left unclear and is only addressed on the next page.

ideas.what: Algebraicity of the inverse of the Lefschetz-type map H^1 -> H^{2n-1}(n-1) via Albanese/Picard and Weil's divisorial correspondences (standard conjecture A/B in degree 1)
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture holds for H^1 (degree ≤ 1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (stated), proofs written by Lieberman (1968) and Kleiman (1968, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures')
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968/69), remark that the conjectures hold in degree 1 via abelian varieties

ideas.what: Criterion: cl(gamma(beta)) on H^1 is an isomorphism iff the induced homomorphism u : A_Y -> B_X is an isogeny
ideas.modern_name: Tate module / H^1 characterization of isogenies
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil / classical theory of abelian varieties

ideas.what: Integral version: the inverse correspondence can be taken with integer coefficients iff u is an isomorphism, with denominators controlled by primes dividing the degree (or exponent) of the isogeny
ideas.modern_name: Integral Lefschetz standard conjecture in degree 1 / denominators of the Lambda operator
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore, consequence of Weil's theorem Hom(Alb_Y, Pic^0_X) = divisorial correspondences

ideas.what: Use of isocrystals (Dieudonné theory) to control the p-part of denominators in characteristic p (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline realisation of correspondences on abelian varieties

missed.claim: Grothendieck tracks integrality and denominators of the algebraic inverse of the Lefschetz operator in degree 1, not just its Q-algebraicity. Denominators are bounded by primes dividing the isogeny degree, and integrality holds iff u is an isomorphism. Integral and torsion questions for standard-conjecture-type operators were only studied much later.
missed.quote: Pour qu'on puisse choisir D à coefficients entiers, il faut et il suffit que u soit un isom. ... peut choisir D de la forme D = N^{-r} D_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral versions of the Lefschetz standard conjecture and denominators of Künneth/Lambda correspondences are current topics (e.g. integral Hodge/Tate-type questions and motives with integral coefficients). This page shows Grothendieck already formulated the degree-1 integral case, though its content is folklore from Weil's theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The main result (standard conjecture in degree 1 via Albanese/Picard) is well known and was stated by Grothendieck himself. The integral/denominator refinement is a mildly interesting unpublished detail but follows readily from Weil's theory of divisorial correspondences.
transcription_corrections: 'a(^tγ(D))' and 'a(γ(β))' are presumably 'cl(...)' (cycle class). The image reads 'a(' but the meaning is the cohomology class map.
'Al(X×Y)⊗Q' = group of cycles modulo algebraic equivalence (A^1 or 'Al').
The 'u_Z^{-1}' line reads 'u_Z' with a superscript resembling '-1' ('u^{-1}_Z').
Margin/struck lines around 'r ≥ 0' are mostly illegible. 'mais pas ≥ 1' is uncertain.
'H^1(B_X,Q_l)': the image has 'H^1(B_X, Q_l)', which is correct; the bottom-left entry is H^1(A_Y,Q_l).
